Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up and next steps

Hey Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier good discussion on expected traffic patterns and compliance needs. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on: 

- Deployment mode: you confirmed leaning toward Dedicated capacity with VPC peering (private networking) good for predictable throughput and data isolation.
- Primary models: mix of open LLMs + a fine-tuned model for clinical triage.
- Performance targets (you mentioned rough numbers on the call): peak TPS ~120, sustained TPS ~60, average concurrency per model ~40-60.
- Token mix: average request ~1.2k tokens (prompt+response), with ~70% of tokens in generation (completion) vs 30% prompt.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target ~300-400ms for generation.
- Procurement: Tom is the procurement lead; we'll share SOW draft and sizing workbook.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (blank workbook with tabs for TPS/concurrency/token mixes) and a first-pass SOW draft (SOW-draft-v0.2.pdf).

Questions we still need from you (helps sizing/quote):
1) Typical QPS distribution (peak hour vs daily average) and any burst patterns (e.g., batch jobs at night).
2) % of requests that require KV cache reuse (long chat sessions vs single-turn).
3) Any hard constraints on GPU type or preference (A100 vs H100) due to internal procurement/policy.

Next steps:
- Can you populate the sizing sheet with sample hourly QPS and token distribution I attached a tab with examples.
- Rafael (cc) will propose an initial GPU topology based on what you send.
- Aditya (cc) can run a short benchmark once we have a sample workload.
- Proposed 30-min follow-up technical call next week to lock sizing.

Thanks talk soon.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers inline and a few clarifications: 

- Deployment mode: Confirmed we want Dedicated capacity with VPC peering.
- TPS/Concurrency: Peak TPS 120 is accurate; sustained TPS ~60. Concurrency target ~50 across models (users open long chat sessions).
- Token mix: average end-to-end per request ~1.2k tokens; roughly 65-75% completion tokens depending on the prompt.
- Latency: 95th percentile target <= 400ms.

I attached a short sample of our usage (acme-usage-sample.csv) showing hourly QPS for the past 30 days. Notably, we have weekday spikes between 09:00-11:00 and 15:00-16:00 PST. There are also nightly batch runs (no more than 5% of traffic) that can be scheduled outside peak hours.

GPU preference: procurement prefers H100-class if available, but we can consider A100 if cost delta is large. Key is meeting the latency SLO.

Procurement contact: Tom Li (cc) will own the SOW and purchase order. He asked that the SOW include an estimate for both H100 and A100 configs.

We'll try to populate the sizing workbook with the sample hourly CSV by EOD Monday.

Perfect — thanks for the data, Samantha. Rafael and I chatted about a recommended baseline while we wait for the full workbook: 

Baseline recommendation (initial quote/sizing):
- GPU: H100 nodes (preferred) with quantization-friendly config where possible. Quote will also include an alternate A100 estimate per Tom's request.
- Pool topology: start with a 6-node H100 pool with autoscaling to 10 nodes for peaks. With your given token mix (1.2k avg) and 50 concurrency, this configuration is estimated to sustain ~60 TPS with headroom to ~140 TPS during short bursts using burst capacity.
- Concurrency & batching: target avg concurrency 50, with per-GPU concurrency tuned by batching and KV cache reuse. We recommend enabling prefix caching for long chat sessions to reduce per-token compute.
- Latency: we expect 95p ~300-450ms depending on prompt lengths; we can tighten this by increasing pool size or moving to denser H100 configs.

Action items for us:
- Rafael will prepare the two-cost scenarios (H100 vs A100) and a preliminary pricing worksheet.
- Aditya will run a micro-benchmark once you provide the populated hourly QPS and a small sample of representative requests.
- Marissa to schedule 30-min technical sizing call (propose Tue 15 Jun 10:00-10:30 PDT).

Tom I'll flag the SOW to include both GPU estimates and notes about VPC peering and compliance (SOC2 logs, KMS integration).

If that sounds good, I'll pencil in the Tue timeslot and send a calendar invite.

Quick technical notes from my side:

- Given the long chat sessions and KV reuse, we should enable prefix/KV caching aggressively; this reduces repeated attention compute and improves effective throughput.
- Quantization: recommend running model variants at 4-bit (where validated) for cost savings, but we'll bench both FP16 and 4-bit paths for accuracy/regression risk.
- Batching: use dynamic batching with a short batching window (6-8ms) to hit latency SLOs while capturing some packing efficiency.
- Bench inputs needed: 1) a sample of 100 representative requests (JSONL) covering short and long sessions; 2) 24-hour QPS histogram (you provided a sample helpful).

I can run a 30-min micro-benchmark once you drop the sample requests into the Drive folder. Please label the file "acme_sample_requests.jsonl" and share the link (or grant access). I will report back with per-GPU TPS, latency p50/p95, and a recommended pool size for H100 vs A100.

Happy to join the Tue sizing call if useful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
